result.rationale: The finding is accurate: topic_embed.rb adds a content_sha1 comparison gate around PostRevisor.revise!, and the update test at spec line 39 only asserts /new contents/ appears in cooked — it never verifies that identical content skips revision or that content_sha1 is updated. The RSS poll runs hourly, so a regression causing repeated revisions would produce silent repeated post revisions/edit-history growth and pass the existing suite. adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, the "Supports updating the post" example only asserts `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/` after calling `TopicEmbed.import` a second time. It does not assert that the existing `TopicEmbed` row’s `content_sha1` was updated (topic_embed.rb updates via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`), that the same post/topic was revised rather than a new one being created (topic_embed.rb branches on `embed.blank?`), or that re-importing identical content skips revision (topic_embed.rb’s `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`). This is a concrete gap in coverage for newly added nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable functional bug in the diff.
